title: Perfect approximations to pseudo-coherent complexes on qcqs schemes
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ be pseudo-coherent [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], and let $a\in\mathbf Z$. There exist a perfect object $P\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-perfect-complex] and a morphism $u:P\to E$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ such that $H^i(u)$ is an isomorphism for every $i>a$ and $H^a(u)$ is surjective. No Noetherian, separated, ample-line-bundle or base-ring hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 08ES, theorem-approximation, with T=X in Tags 08EN (definition-approximation) and 08EM (definition-approximation-holds).

proof.text: For each quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X$, let the property under induction be $\mathsf A(W)$. The affine lemma supplies $\mathsf A(W)$ for every affine open, including the empty scheme.

source.place: Tag 08ES, theorem-approximation, affine base case via Tag 08EQ, lemma-approximation-affine.

proof.text: Consider quasi-compact opens $U,V\subseteq X$ with $V$ affine and suppose the induction hypotheses hold for $U,V,U\cap V$. Quasi-separatedness of $X$ implies that $U\cap V$ is quasi-compact. Apply the open-step lemma to the scheme $U\cup V$ with its two indicated opens and the hypothesis $\mathsf A(U)$ to obtain $\mathsf A(U\cup V)$. Thus the existing quasi-compact-open induction theorem applies and gives $\mathsf A(X)$.

source.place: Tag 08ES, theorem-approximation: Tag 08ER, lemma-induction-step, and coherent.tex Tag 08DR, lemma-induction-principle.

proof.text: By quasi-coherence of pseudo-coherent objects, $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. In $\mathsf A(X)$ choose $T=X$, whose complement is empty and hence retrocompact. Obtain its integer $r$, and put $m=a$. The definition of pseudo-coherence says that $E$ is $(a-r)$-pseudo-coherent, and every support hypothesis outside $T=X$ is vacuous. The defining conclusion of $\mathsf A(X)$ therefore gives a perfect $P$ and $u:P\to E$ with the asserted cohomology isomorphisms and surjection, including the endpoint $a$.

source.place: Tags 08EM and 08EN with T=X, after Tag 08ES; quasi-coherence via Tag 08E5, lemma-pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: The perfect object $P$ has quasi-coherent cohomology, so the same $P$ belongs to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. None of the preceding statements imposed a Noetherian, separated, ample-line-bundle, or base-ring hypothesis.
